llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Carbon ink is treated as the user-supplied deposited analyte and is not added to the electrolyte. Its composition, density, molecular weight, and solids content are not specified, so no concentration or mass calculation is applicable. A 10 uL aliquot is transferred directly to the glassy-carbon disk as requested.
assumptions: Solid KCl is available in a Quantos-compatible cartridge, and water is available on liquid-pump channel 1, as stated in the available materials and hardware.
The carbon ink is available as a user-supplied dispensable sample for the electrode drop-casting operation; it is not assumed to be pump-compatible or dissolved in the electrolyte.

A 3 mm glassy carbon working electrode and compatible holder/connection are physically installed and available. This user-specified electrode differs from the generic electrode choices listed in the base schema and must be accepted by the electrode holder before execution.
The electrochemical substation can perform the specified drop-casting transfer and camera inspection or has an equivalent pipetting/deposition accessory loaded with carbon ink.
The Ag/AgCl reference electrode is filled with 3 M KCl, is serviceable, and has an intact porous junction.
The carbon ink contains no unreported highly hazardous component requiring a special drying or inert-atmosphere protocol. Its supplier safety data sheet must be reviewed before handling.
The 15.0 mL water dispense is the platform-defined preparation volume; the dissolved KCl volume contribution is neglected, as is standard for this automated electrolyte recipe.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Required KCl moles = 0.100 mol/L x 0.0150 L = 0.00150 mol. Required mass = 0.00150 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.11182695 g = 111.82695 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 111.827 mg. Actual concentration from the rounded mass is (0.111827 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.0150 L = 0.10000004 mol/L, effectively 0.100 M.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One solid reagent is used, below the maximum of eight cartridges. KCl mass is 111.827 mg, below the 200 mg capacity of one Quantos cartridge. One pump-compatible liquid is used, below four liquid channels. Water volume is 15.0 mL, satisfying the platform requirement for electrode immersion and the 15 mL final-volume requirement. One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used, below the limits of 31 vials and three parallel slots. KCl is represented as a Quantos-dispensed solid and water as a pump-dispensed liquid. The requested 10 uL carbon-ink deposition, 10 CV cycles, platinum counter electrode, Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode, and -0.20 to +0.80 V potential window are explicitly specified.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: A 1800 second (30 minute) ambient drying period is selected as a conservative default for a 10 uL drop-cast ink film. This minimizes loss of loosely adhered wet material into the electrolyte. If the carbon-ink supplier specifies a different drying temperature, atmosphere, or duration, that validated procedure must replace this default before execution.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Use a clean, dry 3 mm diameter glassy carbon working electrode. Do not perform the platform polishing operation after coating. Pipette 10 uL carbon ink centrally onto the glassy-carbon disk using the electrode-deposition operation, avoiding overflow onto the insulating shroud or electrical contact. Dry for 1800 seconds, then use camera inspection to confirm an intact, dry coating. Immerse the coated working electrode in the prepared KCl electrolyte with a platinum wire counter electrode and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 111.827 mg solid KCl from Quantos cartridge position 1 into one 20 mL experiment vial. Dispense 15.0 mL water into the same vial using liquid channel 1. Mix with a stir bar for 300 seconds, or until no visible KCl crystals remain, before electrode immersion. The electrolyte preparation uses only available solid KCl, water, Quantos solid dispensing, and liquid-pump dispensing.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.10 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte was selected because it provides adequate ionic conductivity and minimizes uncompensated resistance while remaining chemically simple and compatible with an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode. The requested potential limits are retained exactly: start at -0.20 V and scan to a +0.80 V vertex versus Ag/AgCl. A 50 mV/s scan rate is suitable for initial carbon-film characterization because it limits capacitive current and permits observation of coating stabilization over the requested exactly 10 cycles. A 5 mV potential increment gives approximately 200 points over the 1.0 V forward sweep, providing adequate resolution. AUTO current ranging is selected because the capacitance, conductivity, thickness, and electroactive impurity content of the unspecified carbon ink are unknown. No nitrogen purge is selected because this is an initial ambient aqueous carbon-electrode characterization and oxygen-related features may be part of the observed baseline response.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The analyte is carbon ink deposited on, rather than dissolved in, the working electrode. Therefore analyte_on_working_electrode mode is required. The supporting electrolyte is prepared separately in the experiment vial before coating deposition and electrochemical measurement.

metadata.description: Characterize a 10 uL drop-cast carbon ink coating on a 3 mm diameter glassy carbon working electrode by cyclic voltammetry in 15 mL of 0.10 M aqueous KCl using a platinum wire counter electrode and an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Carbon-ink-coated glassy-carbon electrode CV in 0.10 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform CV to characterize carbon deposited (10 uL) onto a glassy carbon working electrode (d = 3 mm). Pipette the carbon ink onto the electrode and allow it to dry. Prepare 15 mL of KCl supporting electrolyte using available solid KCl and water. Immerse the coated electrode and perform CV using a platinum counter electrode and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode. Select a suitable KCl concentration and justified CV settings, starting with a potential window of -0.2 to +0.8 V versus Ag/AgCl and exactly 10 cycles. Verify reagent and hardware availability, follow safety requirements, and return the complete executable configuration in the required JSON schema.

cross_contamination_risks: Carbon ink can contaminate polishing stations, electrode holders, reference junctions, and subsequent electrochemical samples.
A wet or poorly adhered coating may shed carbon into the electrolyte and contaminate the platinum counter electrode or reference-electrode junction.
Use dedicated or thoroughly cleaned deposition tooling for the carbon ink and wash/dry electrode-contact hardware after the test.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and appropriate nitrile gloves while handling KCl, carbon ink, electrodes, and waste.
Load and dispense carbon ink in accordance with its supplier safety data sheet; use suitable ventilation if the ink contains volatile solvent.
Ensure the carbon coating is visibly dry before immersion to avoid dispersing wet ink into the electrolyte.
Keep the Ag/AgCl reference junction and platinum counter electrode immersed without contacting the working electrode or each other.
Do not polish the working electrode after deposition because polishing would remove the carbon coating.
Use camera inspection after drying to confirm that the coating remains on the 3 mm glassy-carbon disk and does not bridge to insulating electrode body materials.
hazards: Potassium chloride is a low-hazard inorganic salt but can cause eye or skin irritation as a solid or concentrated solution.
Carbon ink composition is unspecified and may contain volatile or flammable organic solvent, polymeric binder, and fine carbon particles.
The platinum wire counter electrode, glassy carbon electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode are fragile; damaged electrodes can cause injury or contamination.
Electrical and moving hardware hazards are present during automated electrochemical operation.
waste_disposal: Collect used KCl electrolyte containing detached carbon ink particles as aqueous electrochemical waste; do not return it to the water reservoir.
Dispose of carbon-ink-contaminated wipes, pipette tips, and gloves as solid chemical waste according to the ink safety data sheet and local procedures.
Do not dispose of Ag/AgCl reference-electrode filling solution to drain if it is replaced or leaked; collect as chloride/silver-containing laboratory waste where required.
